rules.reason: Public fetch reaches begin -> plan -> setAlarm. Every nonempty alarm calls plan with the unchanged record; at or after expires-margin the next alarm is now. There is no constructor scheduler, but the reachable alarm feedback itself is sufficient. Reconstructed model instances preserve the same expiry. One pending alarm only bounds simultaneous schedules, not the newly scheduled chain.

expires is never advanced, consumed or checked for terminal expiry by alarm; no persisted allowance, progress, closed state, rate window or stop exists. Eight successful synthetic deliveries kept the same due schedule. These are newly scheduled successful alarms, so a platform exception-retry cap cannot bound the chain.

The supplied top-level config declares one Worker and one SQLite DO class/binding, without env/preview templates or CI. The only visible public path uses literal getByName('one'), with no newUniqueId or caller-controlled identity. This limits known-path object cardinality to one per namespace; external callers, old objects, generated environments and actual preview resource isolation are unverified. No account-wide instance/environment count is asserted.

No explicit SQL/ORM query, cursor, list, join, sort, migration SQL or full scan exists. The DO KV-style get uses one literal key. The SQLite backend is declared via new_sqlite_classes; actual rowsRead/rowsWritten/cache effects are unavailable and stay null. The empty bounded SQLite probe supplies no billing or query-plan evidence.

Every nonempty alarm rewrites the entire unchanged record, then setAlarm writes scheduling metadata. The model counted 9 put and 9 setAlarm calls after begin plus 8 callbacks. Idempotent value equality does not erase storage/scheduling work. There is no wide table update, but this concrete repeated-write path is reachable.
No Cron handler, scheduled trigger, batch, backfill, or bulk maintenance exists in the supplied complete files. The per-object countdown/refresh work is separately reviewed under DO rules.
No Queue producer, consumer, queue binding, external fetch, SDK, or queue feedback edge exists in the complete supplied source/config. This conclusion does not cover independent cloud callers.
No Queue batch, ack/retry, delivery or DLQ is configured or referenced in the supplied artifacts; no missing max_retries field is interpreted as unlimited.
No Workers KV namespace/list/pagination path. DO storage.get/put on literal keys are analyzed as SQLite-backed DO operations rather than Workers KV product usage.
No R2 binding, S3 client, replication/backup dependency, list/head/put path or synchronization configuration in the supplied artifacts.

The default fetch handler ignores method/path/host/credentials and always invokes begin. Local invalid-credential GET and arbitrary-host OPTIONS both reach the DO. There is one fixed stub, with small per-request work; whether this public behavior is intended and which native WAF/admission controls cover workers.dev/custom/preview/internal routes is unverified. No external origin fetch exists, so origin-access is not generated/applicable to these supplied artifacts. Request volume is an assumption, not an enforced global budget.

The supplied code makes no budget-alert/CPU/retry/global-pause claims and uses no invented API. This review distinguishes object runtime deleteAlarm from management/test APIs, does not stop production, reports zero cloud writes, keeps rows/currency unknown, and does not turn singleton routing, a retry limit or the harness cutoff into a monthly hard cap.

findings.native_control_limit: One pending alarm replaces another; successful setAlarm creates future activations outside the exception-retry budget. CPU and incoming WAF controls do not stop this autonomous chain. deleteAlarm is a per-object runtime method and does not cancel running callbacks by itself.
findings.recommendation: Persist a real progress/refresh transition or terminal state before scheduling; require a positive derived next transition and a justified job/window work bound, plus stale-callback/restart stop evidence. Do not delete stored data or invent an account-level DO pause.

findings.native_control_limit: Platform failure retries constrain one failed alarm; these successful callbacks schedule new alarms. The same deterministic object limits known-path cardinality but does not bound its lifetime event count.
findings.recommendation: Prove finite persisted progress or a recurring-service window with enforced rate/work/instance counts and a verifiable durable stop; test the first attempted callback after exhaustion, crashes and restarts.
